title: Predictive Structure Behind Rare Outcomes in Random Quantum Circuits
abstract: Local random quantum circuits selected for unusually large output peaks reveal intermediate-state structure that predicts new peak formation and guides circuit construction. In one-dimensional Haar-random brickwall circuits, the selected trajectories combine stronger pairwise correlations and probability redistribution with lower bipartite entanglement and output entropy. We test the predictive value of this structure by keeping each circuit's initial segment fixed and independently regenerating the remaining gates. Across the tested size-depth grid at n=8-14, peak-selected states have higher new-peak probability than normal/nonpeak controls, with an overall probability ratio of 3.23 at the primary depths. Within a separate unconditioned ensemble, a fixed structural score computed from the initial segment predicts new-peak probability and gives a 1.86-fold yield gain in a replay with equal numbers of remaining-circuit evaluations. Randomizing relative phases while preserving computational-basis probabilities strongly attenuates the selected-state advantage, demonstrating a functional contribution from relative-phase organization. Structural and phase-intervention tests extend to n=16. Structure-guided gate selection improves high-peak yield under common local refinement, while guidance using multiple intermediate observables improves new-peak probability over peak-only guidance in all 16 tested size-depth settings. Together, these results show how intermediate-state structure can predict and promote new peak formation under finite-depth local dynamics.

bite.hook: Hidden intermediate structure in random quantum circuits makes rare, high-probability output peaks predictable.
tldr: Studied 1D Haar-random quantum circuits producing unusually large output probability peaks to detect early internal patterns.
Fixed initial circuit segments, regenerated downstream gates, and tested if intermediate structural scores predicted future peaks.
Found peak-selected circuits yield new peaks at 3.23x the rate of controls, giving an overall 1.86-fold yield gain in search replays.
bite.whyItMatters: Random quantum circuits model chaotic quantum dynamics and underpin quantum supremacy tests. Finding predictable order inside rare outcomes helps researchers design targeted algorithms and systematically synthesize specific quantum states.
bite.eli5: Imagine shaking a giant box of Lego bricks and surprisingly getting a fully assembled tower. Scientists found that halfway through shaking, the bricks quietly snap into special, less messy clusters that make forming the tower far more likely, rather than staying totally random.

glossary.eli5Def: The most perfectly unbiased and uniform way to choose a random quantum operation.
